findings.rationale: Action output gap: actionlint does not reject value on JavaScript action outputs.

Contract difference: SchemaStore requires value on composite action outputs, but the pinned actions/runner schema permits its omission and CompositeActionHandler.ProcessOutputs only sets an output when TryGetValue("value", ...) succeeds. Missing value does not fail this runner path. No additional GitHub service restriction has been established.
Empty-input contract difference: the upstream expression parser accepts empty input as null; actionlint requires an expression.

The runner lexer uses Char.IsWhiteSpace, which includes U+00A0; actionlint recognizes only space, newline, carriage return, and tab. The shared fixture skips TypeScript. This assessment concerns runner compatibility; no live service probe is claimed.
The retired actions/checkout@v3 runtime is an independent lifecycle finding.

Expression literal gap: actionlint does not recognize NaN or Infinity literals accepted by the upstream expression corpus. The checked-in service and runner probes in docs/expression-results/2026-09-14.md confirm these literal spellings.

Runtime attribution pending: actionlint accepts negative hexadecimal -0xFF while the reference parser rejects it. This recorded parser disagreement alone does not establish the GitHub service contract.

Expression numeric syntax gap: leading-dot decimals, unary plus, octal prefixes, and some hexadecimal spellings differ from the upstream lexer. The checked-in service and runner probes cover leading-dot decimals, unary plus, and lowercase octal prefixes; the remaining leading-zero hex forms are accepted by the pinned expression corpus.
Expression syntax gap: actionlint accepts dot wildcards but does not parse bracket wildcards such as items[*].
Extra expression type check: a whole steps object is interpolated into a string.
Extra expression type check: the fixture references an undeclared steps.foo property.
Extra lifecycle check: the fixture uses the retired windows-2019 runner label.
Extra lifecycle checks: these historical fixtures remain parser-valid, while actionlint reports their deprecated or retired action runtimes.
Extra lint checks: cmd is used on Linux and github.test is not a known context property.
Extra lint checks: constant conditions and a reference to an undeclared step are accepted by this reader fixture.
Extra lint checks: empty environment names and references to missing step outputs are accepted by this reader fixture.
Extra lint checks: misleading and constant conditions, incompatible runner labels, and a placeholder runner label are accepted by this serialization fixture.
Extra lint checks: the fixture uses arbitrary runner labels without configuring them as self-hosted labels.
Extra lint checks: the reader accepts incomplete jobs and string coercion in cancel-in-progress; actionlint requires steps and a boolean expression. A retired action is also reported.
Extra matrix check: the YAML scalar reader fixtures deliberately contain equivalent values; actionlint reports duplicate matrix entries after resolving their YAML types.
Extra typo check: the reader ignores unknown workflow_dispatch keys; actionlint reports them.
Fixture reference differs from documented workflow-call syntax: the owner begins with a dot. actionlint rejects that uses reference.

Mixed reader differences: missing steps, undefined matrix and step properties, numeric expression type checks, and github.event.number on a push trigger. The pinned OpenAPI push payload has no number member. The reader accepts the expression syntactically; the payload finding is additional lint feedback, not a claim that GitHub rejects the workflow.

Mixed numeric-field difference: the fixture combines nonfinite expression literals, numeric overflow, and nonfinite timeout values. Literal support is a known actionlint gap, but this fixture does not establish that nonfinite timeouts are valid. It is also skipped by the TypeScript reference implementation; attribution of the whole fixture remains unassessed.
Reader versus expression type validation: cancel-timeout-minutes evaluates a string-valued github.sha where a number is required.
Reader versus lint policy: this fixture uses the retired windows-2019 runner label.
Reader fixture versus lint checks: combined include/exclude filters, retired events, one-minute schedules, and required inputs with defaults produce additional diagnostics.
Reader versus lint checks: constant conditions and unknown context properties produce diagnostics. Empty and YAML-null conditions normalize to success() and agree with the reader.

Resolution boundary: the upstream fixture supplies remote reusable workflows to a mock file provider. actionlint analyzes the caller offline and does not resolve those remote bodies, permissions, or nested calls.

Adapter limits: these fixtures depend on remote workflow expansion, a fixture-specific max-result-size, or the reader expression-length limit. The adapter neither supplies remote workflow bodies nor reproduces the complete reader limit configuration, so these acceptance differences are not scored as proven actionlint runtime defects.
Schema versus lint contract: this JavaScript action fixture omits description and uses node12; actionlint requires a description and reports the retired runtime.

Reference syntax-support gap: the shared insert.yml fixture explicitly skips TypeScript. Actionlint supports the working insert directive and still diagnoses its undeclared steps.set-matrix reference. The shared reader expectation is not evidence that actions/languageservices implements insertion.
The fixture references an undeclared steps.set-matrix property; this finding is independent of insertion support.
Validation gap: actionlint does not check the organization/enterprise prefix of runs-on group names.
Validation gap: the reader reserves job IDs beginning with two underscores; actionlint currently accepts them.
Workflow-call validation gap: actionlint accepts the non-YAML filename that SchemaStore rejects.
